biological.citation: Structural architecture of the human NALCN channelosome (PMID: 34929720)
biological.summary: Cryo-EM structure of the ~1-MDa NALCN channelosome reveals that UNC79 and UNC80 are massive HEAT-repeat proteins forming an intertwined anti-parallel superhelical assembly that docks intracellularly onto the NALCN-FAM155A pore-forming subcomplex. Calmodulin copurifies bound to the C-terminal domain of NALCN, identifying it as a putative modulatory hub. Single-channel analyses uncovered a low open probability for the wild-type complex, with key constraints between UNC79-UNC80 and NALCN DI-DII and DII-DIII linkers informing a model of channelosome gating.

biological.citation: Structure of the human sodium leak channel NALCN (PMID: 32698188)
biological.summary: Cryo-EM structure of NALCN in complex with FAM155A shows that FAM155A forms an extracellular dome shielding the ion-selectivity filter from neurotoxin attack, and the channel has a tightly closed pore gate with occluded lateral fenestrations. Unusual voltage-sensor domains with asymmetric linkages to the pore suggest mechanisms for activity modulation. The majority of missense patient mutations causing gain-of-function phenotypes cluster around the S6 gate and distinctive π-bulges.

biological.citation: Forward-genetics analysis of sleep in randomly mutagenized mice (PMID: 27806374)
biological.summary: A missense gain-of-function mutation in NALCN identified by EEG/EMG-based forward genetic screen in randomly mutagenized mice reduces total amount and episode duration of REM sleep, apparently by increasing the excitability of REM sleep-inhibiting neurons. This demonstrates a role for NALCN in regulating the amount of REM sleep in vivo.

biological.citation: The NALCN channel regulates metastasis and nonmalignant cell dissemination (PMID: 36175792)
biological.summary: Deletion of Nalcn from gastric, intestinal, or pancreatic adenocarcinoma mouse models did not alter tumor incidence but markedly increased circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and metastases. Strikingly, deletion of Nalcn from non-tumor-bearing mice caused shedding of normal epithelial cells into the blood at levels equivalent to tumor-bearing animals, with these cells forming normal structures in distant organs, demonstrating NALCN regulates cell shedding from solid tissues independent of cancer.
biological.sample_size: 10022 human cancers analyzed; multiple mouse models

biological.citation: The NALCN Channel Regulator UNC-80 Functions in a Subset of Interneurons To Regulate Caenorhabditis elegans Reversal Behavior (PMID: 31690562)
biological.summary: Forward genetic screen in C. elegans identified multiple loss-of-function mutations in unc-80 and unc-79 causing defective avoidance response to methyl salicylate; NALCN mutants showed the same phenotype. Neuron-specific rescue and knockdown experiments demonstrated that command interneurons AVA and AVE and guidepost neuron AVG are sufficient for unc-80 regulation of reversal behavior, providing the first identification of key neurons in which the NALCN channelosome functions.

biological.citation: Progesterone and estrogen regulate NALCN expression in human myometrial smooth muscle cells (PMID: 31935111)
biological.summary: In human myometrial smooth muscle cells (MSMCs), NALCN mRNA decreased 2.3-fold with estrogen (E2) and increased 5.6-fold with progesterone (P4) treatment; protein expression followed the same pattern. Progesterone response elements (PREs), but not estrogen response elements, in the NALCN promoter contributed to this regulation as shown by luciferase assays, and E2/P4 correspondingly inhibited/enhanced an NALCN-dependent leak current in MSMCs.

biological.citation: NALCN-mediated sodium influx confers metastatic prostate cancer cell invasiveness (PMID: 37278161)
biological.summary: NALCN is overexpressed in metastatic prostate cancer cells and acts as a major initiator of Ca2+ oscillations required for invadopodia formation. NALCN-mediated Na+ influx maintains intracellular Ca2+ oscillations via plasmalemmal and mitochondrial Na+/Ca2+ exchangers, SERCA, and store-operated channels, promoting Src kinase activity, actin remodeling, and secretion of proteolytic enzymes, thereby increasing invasive potential and metastatic lesions in vivo.

biological.citation: The NALCN ion channel is a new actor in pancreatic β-cell physiology (PMID: 21099296)
biological.summary: NALCN is expressed in rodent islets of Langerhans and the mouse MIN6 pancreatic β-cell line, where it mediates a cation current triggered by acetylcholine activation of M3 muscarinic receptors. The activation mechanism is independent of G protein action but dependent on a Src family kinase (SFK) pathway, and involves co-inclusion of M3 muscarinic receptors and NALCN in the same complex, revealing a novel role for NALCN in pancreatic β-cell excitability.

biological.citation: NALCN expression is down-regulated and associated with immune infiltration in gastric cancer (PMID: 40013144)
biological.summary: NALCN expression was significantly downregulated in gastric cancer (GC) tumor tissues and plasma compared to adjacent non-tumor tissues and healthy controls. NALCN knockdown in AGS and GES-1 GC cell lines markedly enhanced cell proliferation, colony formation, and migration while reducing apoptosis. TCGA analysis showed NALCN expression positively correlated with infiltration of B cells and CD8+ T cells and negatively with Th17 and Th2 cells; co-culture experiments showed NALCN knockdown in GC cells inhibited T cell proliferation.

biological.citation: A new neurodevelopmental disorder linked to heterozygous variants in UNC79 (PMID: 37183800)
biological.summary: Drosophila with UNC79 knocked down displayed an induced seizure-like phenotype, and heterozygous loss-of-function UNC79 mice showed developmental delay in body weight and impaired learning and memory, supporting the role of the NALCN channelosome (NALCN, UNC79, UNC80, FAM155A) in neurological function. Six unrelated patients with heterozygous UNC79 loss-of-function variants presented with intellectual disability, developmental delay, behavioral issues, and epilepsy.
